sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐秘的事”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the heart of the Caribbean, there is a tiny little island called Anguilla.
sentences.zh: 在加勒比海的正中央，有一个叫安圭拉的小岛。

sentences.en: And I mean tiny.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的很小。

sentences.en: At its widest point, it's only about 16 miles across.
sentences.zh: 它最宽的地方也只有大约16英里。

sentences.en: But while it's small, its white sandy beaches and crystal blue waters have made it
sentences.zh: 虽然它很小，但这里洁白的沙滩和清澈湛蓝的海水使它

sentences.en: one of the most desirable tourist destinations in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 成为了加勒比海最令人向往的旅游胜地之一。

sentences.en: It's got all-inclusive resorts, and you can swim with dolphins.
sentences.zh: 这里有全包式度假村，你还可以和海豚一起游泳。

sentences.en: The island is, like, the ideal place to film an episode of The Bachelor.
sentences.zh: 这个小岛简直是拍摄《单身汉》节目的理想地点。

sentences.en: In fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: Tonight on The Bachelor,
sentences.zh: 今晚的《单身汉》节目中，

sentences.en: they did.
sentences.zh: 他们真的这么做了。

sentences.en: Season 15, Week 7.
sentences.zh: 第15季，第7集。

sentences.en: But back in the 1960s, Anguilla didn't have any of the beachside villas or luxury spas or golf courses that it has today.
sentences.zh: 但在20世纪60年代，安圭拉并没有如今那些海滨别墅、豪华水疗中心或高尔夫球场。

sentences.en: It had dirt roads, no electricity, one stoplight in the middle of town.
sentences.zh: 这里只有土路、没有电，镇中心只有一个红绿灯。

sentences.en: That's Emily Oberman.
sentences.zh: 那是艾米莉·奥伯曼。

sentences.en: She used to visit the island on family vacations as a kid.
sentences.zh: 她小时候经常随家人来这个岛上度假。

sentences.en: When you wanted to get a message to someone, you pinned it to this very specific mahogany tree in the center of town in the valley.
sentences.zh: 当你想要给某人传话时，你会把它钉在山谷镇中心那棵特别的红木树上。

sentences.en: Emily's parents were successful graphic designers from New York City, and they liked to travel off the beaten path.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉的父母是来自纽约市成功的平面设计师，他们喜欢去人迹罕至的地方旅游。

sentences.en: This was particularly true for her father, Marvin.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲马尔文尤其如此。

sentences.en: My father was incredibly gregarious and charming and smart and quick-witted and a total wise-ass.
sentences.zh: 我父亲极其热情、迷人、聪明、机智，而且是个彻头彻尾的机灵鬼。

sentences.en: And he always was ready to take someone in his arms and dance with them.
sentences.zh: 他总是随时准备把别人拥入怀中，跟他们一起跳舞。

sentences.en: You can tell Emily loves her dad a lot.
sentences.zh: 看得出来艾米莉非常爱她的爸爸。

sentences.en: Both were parents, really.
sentences.zh: 真的，他们俩都是好父母。

sentences.en: She is an extremely successful graphic designer in her own right, but she gives her parents the credit.
sentences.zh: 她自己本身就是一位非常成功的平面设计师，但她把功劳归于父母。

sentences.en: Abso-friggin-lutely.
sentences.zh: 千真万确。

sentences.en: I am a graphic designer because of my parents.
sentences.zh: 我成为平面设计师完全是因为我的父母。

sentences.en: After her dad passed away in 2018, it was actually a graphic that he helped design that got Emily thinking about Anguilla again.
sentences.zh: 在她父亲于2018年去世后，正是他参与设计的一幅平面图形让艾米莉再次想起了安圭拉。

sentences.en: My father had recently passed, and so I had gone through a bunch of his stuff and came across, you know, a small flag.
sentences.zh: 我父亲最近刚去世，所以我整理了他的一些物品，然后发现了一面，你知道的，小旗子。

sentences.en: The flag was all white with a thin strip of brilliant turquoise blue at the bottom and three orange dolphins arranged in a continuous circle in the center,
sentences.zh: 这面旗子通体白色，底部有一条细细的亮青蓝色条纹，中心排列着三只首尾相连的橙色海豚，

sentences.en: almost like a recycling sign, but, you know, with dolphins.
sentences.zh: 有点像回收标志，不过，你知道的，换成了海豚。

sentences.en: Emily knew that her father had gotten involved with the design on one of their trips to Anguilla and that it had actually flown there for a couple of years.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉知道她的父亲在他们去安圭拉旅行时参与了旗帜的设计，而且这面旗子确实在那里飘扬过几年。

sentences.en: So four decades later, inspired by this keepsake,
sentences.zh: 因此，四十年后，在这个纪念物的启发下，

sentences.en: she decided to take a trip back to Anguilla to honor her father and show her own family this place that had been so important to her childhood.
sentences.zh: 她决定再次前往安圭拉，以纪念她的父亲，并向她自己的家人展示这个对她的童年如此重要的地方。

sentences.en: I hadn't been there in 40 years, so it was going to be an adventure and an experience for me,
sentences.zh: 我已经40年没去那里了，所以对我和我的经历来说这将是一次冒险，

sentences.en: but I thought probably an emotional one because it had been so meaningful to my family.
sentences.zh: 但我想这可能也会充满情感，因为它对我的家庭意义重大。

sentences.en: In April of 2019, Emily packed up her husband and sons and they schlepped through the cold to Newark Airport, hopped on a plane to St. Martin, where they boarded a ferry.
sentences.zh: 在2019年4月，艾米莉收拾好丈夫和儿子的行囊，在严寒中艰难前往纽瓦克机场，搭乘飞机前往圣马丁岛，并在那里登上了渡轮。

sentences.en: And as we were approaching, there was a big sign welcoming you to Anguilla and it was on a white building with orange and turquoise typography.
sentences.zh: 当我们接近时，有一个大招牌欢迎你来到安圭拉，它在一栋白色的建筑上，带有橙色和青绿色的字体。

sentences.en: And I looked at it and thought, huh, that's cool.
sentences.zh: 我看着它想，嗯，这挺酷的。

sentences.en: I recognize those colors.
sentences.zh: 我认得这些颜色。

sentences.en: They were the same colors as her father's flag, orange, white and blue.
sentences.zh: 它们和她父亲旗帜上的颜色一样：橙色、白色和蓝色。

sentences.en: And she noticed them a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且她频繁地注意到这些颜色。

sentences.en: I suddenly began to see the color scheme was everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我突然开始发现这种配色方案无处不在。

sentences.en: The pylons along the highway had those three colors painted on them.
sentences.zh: 公路两旁的柱子上都涂着这三种颜色。

sentences.en: And the color theme was just everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这种色彩主题简直随处可见。

sentences.en: So it was a little bit of a surprise and a delight.
sentences.zh: 所以这既有点意外，又让人感到惊喜。

sentences.en: Emily's father was an amateur writer.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉的父亲是一位业余作家。

sentences.en: So when Emily returned home from her trip, she looked through his folder of stories to see if she could find out more about this flag.
sentences.zh: 因此，当艾米莉旅行归来后，她翻阅了他的一堆故事手稿，看看能否找到更多关于这面旗子的信息。

sentences.en: We looked through his stories and sure enough, there was the story of the Anguillian flag.
sentences.zh: 我们翻阅了他的故事，果不其然，里面记录了安圭拉旗帜的故事。

sentences.en: It turns out that her father's dolphin flag was a bigger deal than Emily had realized and that her parents, a couple of graphic designers from New York City,
sentences.zh: 原来她父亲的海豚旗比艾米莉意识到的要重要得多，而且她的父母——这对来自纽约市的平面设计师夫妇——

sentences.en: had played a very small but not insignificant role in a key moment in the island's history.
sentences.zh: 在岛上历史的关键时刻发挥了微小但绝不 insignificant（微不足道）的作用。

sentences.en: Because this flag that had been collecting dust in the family attic was a symbol of one of history's strangest political revolutions.
sentences.zh: 因为这面在家庭阁楼里积灰的旗子，正是历史上最离奇的政治革命之一的象征。

sentences.en: When I was born, there were dirt roads, no running water, no telephone.
sentences.zh: 当我出生的时候，这里只有泥土路，没有自来水，也没有电话。

sentences.en: This is Timothy Hodge, former president of the Anguilla Archaeological and Historical Society.
sentences.zh: 这是蒂莫西·霍奇，安圭拉考古与历史学会前会长。

sentences.en: Like Emily Oberman, he was a kid in the 1960s and he remembers the island a lot like she does.
sentences.zh: 就像艾米莉·奥伯曼一样，他也是20世纪60年代的一个孩子，他对这个岛的记忆和她很像。

sentences.en: None of the comforts that we have today.
sentences.zh: 没有我们今天拥有的任何舒适设施。

sentences.en: Very little commerce, very little employment.
sentences.zh: 商业活动极少，就业机会极少。

sentences.en: Anguilla had been one of Great Britain's many overseas colonies since the 1650s.
sentences.zh: 自17世纪50年代以来，安圭拉一直是英国的众多海外殖民地之一。

sentences.en: But unlike many of Britain's other territories, Anguilla was missing a lot of essential services like electricity, paved roads, proper schools,
sentences.zh: 但与英国的许多其他领土不同，安圭拉缺乏许多基本服务，如电力、铺面道路、像样的学校，

sentences.en: mostly because the British neglected it.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为英国人忽视了它。

sentences.en: Basically, if you read the historical records, it was not recognized as having any value to the British crown.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果你阅读历史记录，它被认为对英国王室没有任何价值。

sentences.en: So nobody paid any attention to it.
sentences.zh: 所以没有人关注它。

sentences.en: Even though the island has a history of slavery, Anguilla's soil wasn't fertile enough for large-scale agriculture.
sentences.zh: 尽管该岛有奴隶制的历史，但安圭拉的土壤不够肥沃，无法进行大规模农业。

sentences.en: And according to Hodge, if the British couldn't establish widespread slave plantations on Anguilla, then they didn't have much use for it.
sentences.zh: 据霍奇所说，如果英国人不能在安圭拉建立广泛的奴隶种植园，那么他们对这个岛就没有多大用处。

sentences.en: And so for decades, centuries even, they basically ignored the island, which meant Anguilla got very little funding for development.
sentences.zh: 因此几十年来，甚至几个世纪以来，他们基本上忽视了这个岛，这意味着安圭拉几乎没有得到发展资金。

sentences.en: It was just an island that was unto itself, existed unto itself.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个孤立的岛屿，独立存在着。

sentences.en: And this is the Anguilla that existed up until from 1650, when it was settled initially, to 1825.
sentences.zh: 这就是从1650年最初定居到1825年期间存在的安圭拉。

sentences.en: But in 1825, Britain decided just to throw some of the smaller islands together to form a single colony.
sentences.zh: 但在1825年，英国决定将一些较小的岛屿拼凑在一起，组成一个单一的殖民地。

sentences.en: Anguilla would be treated as one part of a multi-island colony, along with St. Kitts, which is also known as St. Christopher, and eventually with Nevis,
sentences.zh: 安圭拉将被视为多岛殖民地的一部分，与圣基茨（也称为圣克里斯托弗）以及后来的尼维斯一起，

sentences.en: with St. Kitts in administrative control of the Union.
sentences.zh: 由圣基茨对该联盟进行行政控制。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Anguilla went from essentially independent self-governance to having to answer to St. Kitts for everything.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，安圭拉从基本上独立的自治状态变成了一切都要向圣基茨汇报。

sentences.en: Without consulting the people of Anguilla, Britain decided to lump it with St. Kitts and Nevis.
sentences.zh: 在没有咨询安圭拉人民的情况下，英国决定把它和圣基茨及尼维斯捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: This is Don Walachek.
sentences.zh: 这是唐·瓦拉切克。

sentences.en: He studies Caribbean history at the University of Puerto Rico.
sentences.zh: 他在波多黎各大学研究加勒比海历史。

sentences.en: He says this was a common move for the British in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 他说这是英国在加勒比地区的常见做法。

sentences.en: Just like it lumped together other countries like Trinidad and Tobago, Antigua and Barbuda, Cariacou and Grenada.
sentences.zh: 就像它把特立尼达和多巴哥、安提瓜和巴布达、卡里亚库和格林纳达等其他国家拼凑在一起一样。

sentences.en: So there were other examples of this.
sentences.zh: 所以还有其他这样的例子。

sentences.en: But there was one huge problem with lumping Anguilla with St. Kitts.
sentences.zh: 但把安圭拉和圣基茨捆绑在一起有一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: The Anguillians didn't like the Kittsians.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉人不喜欢圣基茨人。

sentences.en: You know, it's just a match that was never made in heaven.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这简直是一段天底下最不般配的姻缘。

sentences.en: St. Kitts and Anguilla were two very, very different islands with very different relationships with Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 圣基茨和安圭拉是两个非常非常不同的岛屿，与英国的关系也截然不同。

sentences.en: One of the gripes that the Anguillian people had was that the aid that came to the colony always ended up in St. Kitts.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉人抱怨的事情之一，就是提供给殖民地的援助总是落入圣基茨手中。

sentences.en: So that St. Kitts had electricity and running water and telephones and the things that we spoke about that Anguilla didn't have.
sentences.zh: 因此圣基茨有电、有自来水、有电话，还有我们刚才说的安圭拉没有的东西。

sentences.en: And at the time, Anguilla's leaders were calling for things like piers and, you know, a better port.
sentences.zh: 当时，安圭拉的领导人正呼吁修建防波堤和更好的港口。

sentences.en: There was a story going around at the time that the leader of St. Kitts had been given money by Britain to build a much needed Anguillian pier.
sentences.zh: 当时流传着这样一个故事：英国曾给圣基茨领导人资金，用来修建安圭拉急需的防波堤。

sentences.en: But instead of building it on Anguilla, he actually built the pier in St. Kitts and called it the Anguilla pier.
sentences.zh: 但他没有把防波堤建在安圭拉，而是在圣基茨建了防波堤，并把它叫做安圭拉防波堤。

sentences.en: Tension between the two islands simmered for over a century until 1967, when Britain made a decision that would turn their feud into an open conflict.
sentences.zh: 两岛之间的紧张局势酝酿了一个多世纪，直到1967年，英国做出一个决定，将他们的争端变成了公开冲突。

sentences.en: Rather than separating the two islands as Anguillians wanted, the British government decided that St. Kitts, Nevis and Anguilla wouldn't be a single colony anymore,
sentences.zh: 英国政府没有像安圭拉人希望的那样将两岛分离，而是决定圣基茨、尼维斯和安圭拉不再是一个单独的殖民地，

sentences.en: but an official, self-governing, associated state with St. Kitts in charge.
sentences.zh: 而是一个官方的、自治的联系国，由圣基茨负责领导。

sentences.en: Which, I know, basically sounds like the same thing, but Hodge says this arrangement was much worse.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这听起来基本上是一回事，但霍奇说这种安排要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: At least with the colony status, they could complain to somebody, they could complain to Britain, but after that they would have nobody to complain to.
sentences.zh: 至少在殖民地地位下，他们还可以向某人抱怨，他们可以向英国抱怨，但在此之后他们将无可诉苦。

sentences.en: Anguillians were now entirely at the mercy of St. Kitts, and they started protesting immediately.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉人现在完全受制于圣基茨，他们立刻开始抗议。

sentences.en: The entire police force on Anguilla was made up of 17 ketitions, and they became the symbol of ketition authority.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉整个警察部队由17名圣基茨人组成，他们成为了圣基茨权威的象征。

sentences.en: So, in February of 1967, Anguillian rebels rounded up all 17 officers and booted them off the island.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1967年2月，安圭拉叛军将所有17名警官集中起来，把他们赶出了小岛。

sentences.en: They took the police, they took their weapons, and they put them onto vessels and shipped them off to St. Kitts and said,
sentences.zh: 他们带走了警察，带走了他们的武器，把他们装上船送往圣基茨，并说道：

sentences.en: well, we are forever free of you, and we are separate and independent from you.
sentences.zh: “嗯，我们永远摆脱你们了，我们与你们分道扬镳、各自独立。”

sentences.en: This was the first act in the Anguillian Revolution, one of many revolutions that were happening throughout the British Empire at the time.
sentences.zh: 这是安圭拉革命的第一幕，也是当时席卷整个大英帝国的众多革命之一。

sentences.en: Jamaica becomes the first nation in the Western Hemisphere to gain independence.
sentences.zh: 牙买加成为西半球第一个获得独立的国家。

sentences.en: August the 15th, 1947, Independence Day for India.
sentences.zh: 1947年8月15日，印度的独立日。

sentences.en: These are among the last pictures to be taken in the capital of the Gold CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 这些是在黄金海岸首都拍摄的最后几张照片之一。

sentences.en: For when this day is over, a crowd...
sentences.zh: 因为当这一天结束时，人群……

sentences.en: And now Anguilla II was declaring their independence.
sentences.zh: 现在安圭拉人也要宣布独立了。

sentences.en: Kind of.
sentences.zh: 算是吧。

sentences.en: The Anguilla Revolution in 1967 caused lots of historians and others to scratch their heads.
sentences.zh: 1967年的安圭拉革命让许多历史学家和其他人感到困惑。

sentences.en: Because Anguilla was calling for independence from St. Kitts and dependence on Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 因为安圭拉呼吁脱离圣基茨独立，并转而依赖英国。

sentences.en: The island wanted to go back to being ruled directly by the British.
sentences.zh: 这个岛屿希望回到直接受英国统治的状态。

sentences.en: Really and truly what the Anguillians had asked for was to be ruled directly from Britain.
sentences.zh: 实际上，安圭拉人真正要求的，是由英国直接统治。

sentences.en: They figured it was better to be loosely ruled by a country half a world away than tightly policed by your next-door neighbor.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，受半个地球之外的国家松散统治，总比被隔壁邻居严密监管要好。

sentences.en: As all this was going on, a young Emily Oberman and her family were on one of their trips to Anguilla.
sentences.zh: 正当这一切发生时，年轻的艾米莉·奥伯曼和她的家人正在安圭拉进行他们的又一次旅行。

sentences.en: Emily's father Marvin learned about the conflict over breakfast when he overheard two men recounting a raid on the police station.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉的父亲马尔文在吃早餐时偶然听到两个男人在讲述对警察局的袭击，从而得知了这场冲突。

sentences.en: They said that there was an attack on the police station.
sentences.zh: 他们说警察局遭到了一次袭击。

sentences.en: And one of the guys apparently was very proud that he had shot two bullets.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人显然为自己开了两枪而感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: But the police station was closed at the time.
sentences.zh: 但当时警察局是关门的。

sentences.en: So there was...
sentences.zh: 所以有……

sentences.en: He was just shooting two bullets at an empty building.
sentences.zh: 他只是朝着一栋空建筑开了两枪。

sentences.en: Curious, Marvin Oberman started asking around.
sentences.zh: 出于好奇，马尔文·奥伯曼开始四处打听。

sentences.en: What were these guys talking about?
sentences.zh: 这些人究竟在谈论什么？

sentences.en: Why would there be a raid on the police station?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有人袭击警察局？

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底怎么回事？

sentences.en: He was eventually introduced to a man named Jeremiah Gumbs, who was able to explain the revolution.
sentences.zh: 他最终被介绍认识了一位名叫耶利米·冈布斯的人，他向马尔文解释了这场革命。

sentences.en: Because he was involved.
sentences.zh: 因为他参与其中。

sentences.en: I mean, Jeremiah Gumbs...
sentences.zh: 我是说，耶利米·冈布斯……

sentences.en: I say Jeremiah Gumbs was a colossus.
sentences.zh: 我说耶利米·冈布斯是个巨人。

sentences.en: This is Alan Gumbs, son of Jeremiah Gumbs.
sentences.zh: 这是艾伦·冈布斯，耶利米·冈布斯的儿子。

sentences.en: He was as strong as any man I've known.
sentences.zh: 他是我见过的最强壮的人之一。

sentences.en: And physically, his closest thing in physical stature was the American athlete Jim Brown.
sentences.zh: 从体型上来说，他最接近的美国运动员是吉姆·布朗。

sentences.en: But, I mean, he was like solid steel and he could run and he could do everything in the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他就像坚固的钢铁一样，能跑能跳，无所不能。

sentences.en: Jeremiah had moved away to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 耶利米在20多岁时搬到了美国，

sentences.en: in his 20s, but had come back to Anguilla with his wife Lydia to open up a hotel.
sentences.zh: 但后来和妻子莉迪亚一起回到了安圭拉开了一家酒店。

sentences.en: He didn't have any official role in the government, but he became deeply involved in the politics of the island.
sentences.zh: 他在政府中没有担任任何官方职务，但却深深卷入了该岛的政治。

sentences.en: They even gave him the nickname, the Roving Ambassador.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至给他起了个绰号叫“流动大使”。

sentences.en: He was very involved in where the revolution was going and how it was going to be handled.
sentences.zh: 他非常关心革命的发展方向以及将如何处理。

sentences.en: And I think he had a better eye for even publicity.
sentences.zh: 我认为他甚至更有宣传眼光。

sentences.en: Jeremiah and Lydia knew that if this revolution was going to capture people's imagination, they needed a good flag.
sentences.zh: 耶利米和莉迪亚知道，如果这场革命要激起人们的想象力，他们就需要一面好旗帜。

sentences.en: The original idea was for Anguilla to...
sentences.zh: 最初的想法是安圭拉要……

sentences.en: it was going to break away.
sentences.zh: 它要脱离出去。

sentences.en: And so they had to have a flag.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须有一面旗子。

sentences.en: It isn't entirely clear whether the Gumbs reached out to Marvin or if Marvin reached out to them.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不完全清楚是冈布斯一家联系了马尔文，还是马尔文联系了他们。

sentences.en: But one way or another, Emily's father helped create a whole new flag for a whole new political future.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，艾米莉的父亲帮助为一个全新的政治未来创造了一面崭新的旗帜。

sentences.en: The idea behind the flag was that he wanted it to be incredibly simple.
sentences.zh: 这面旗帜背后的理念是，他希望它极其简单。

sentences.en: As any good flag should be.
sentences.zh: 正如任何好旗帜应有的那样。

sentences.en: Marvin drew inspiration from the colors of the island itself.
sentences.zh: 马尔文从安圭拉岛本身的色彩中汲取了灵感。

sentences.en: Pretty much wherever you are on Anguilla, you can see this beautiful turquoise water.
sentences.zh: 在安圭拉，几乎无论你在哪里，都能看到这片美丽的青绿色海水。

sentences.en: And the idea of there being a long band across the bottom certainly felt like what a flag should have.
sentences.zh: 底部有一条长长的色带这种设计，确实符合人们对旗帜的直观想象。

sentences.en: Like in the vocabulary of flags, there should be a big wide band of something and an iconic image of something else.
sentences.zh: 就像在旗帜的视觉语言中，应该有一大块宽阔的色带和另一个标志性的图案。

sentences.en: Lydia Gumbs and Marvin settled on three colors.
sentences.zh: 莉迪亚·冈布斯和马尔文最终敲定了三种颜色。

sentences.en: White, blue, and orange.
sentences.zh: 白色、蓝色和橙色。

sentences.en: White for peace and tranquility.
sentences.zh: 白色象征和平与宁静。

sentences.en: The blue base representing the surrounding sea and also faith and hope.
sentences.zh: 蓝色的底色代表周围的大海，也代表信念和希望。

sentences.en: And the three orange dolphins at the center, which symbolized endurance, strength, and unity in a perpetual circle.
sentences.zh: 中央的三只橙色海豚，象征着在永恒的循环中展现出的坚韧、力量和团结。

sentences.en: You know, the recycling circle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，回收循环。

sentences.en: Marvin coordinated with Lydia from his office in New York and mocked up a prototype.
sentences.zh: 马文与他在纽约办公室的莉迪亚进行协调，并制作了一个原型。

sentences.en: But since he was technically working for a government in revolt, he had some concerns.
sentences.zh: 但由于他技术上是在为叛乱政府工作，他有一些顾虑。

sentences.en: My father was so nervous about designing this flag.
sentences.zh: 我父亲在设计这面旗帜时非常紧张。

sentences.en: He was petrified that he was being followed by the FBI because he was working for a foreign government in revolt.
sentences.zh: 他吓坏了，因为他认为自己正在被联邦调查局追踪，因为他在为外国叛乱政府工作。

sentences.en: So he was sure that MI5 was following him or the FBI.
sentences.zh: 所以他确信军情五处或联邦调查局在跟踪他。

sentences.en: And he would keep the shades drawn in his office.
sentences.zh: 而且他会在办公室里一直拉着窗帘。

sentences.en: And it was actually hilariously charming.
sentences.zh: 而且这其实非常滑稽可爱。

sentences.en: It turns out that the FBI had very little interest in Marvin's flag project.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，联邦调查局对马文的旗帜项目几乎没有兴趣。

sentences.en: And he was able to get the prototype printed without issue.
sentences.zh: 他顺利地印出了原型。

sentences.en: And they made the flag, which my father then wrapped in something, wrapped in something, and brought to Jerry and Lydia Gumbs.
sentences.zh: 他们制作了这面旗帜，然后我父亲把它包起来，包好后带给了杰里和莉迪亚·甘布斯。

sentences.en: And that was the first flag.
sentences.zh: 那就是第一面旗帜。

sentences.en: The flag with the three dolphins.
sentences.zh: 那面带有三只海豚的旗帜。

sentences.en: That flag suddenly caught on.
sentences.zh: 那面旗帜突然流行起来。

sentences.en: And it has remained loved and beloved by the Anguillian people.
sentences.zh: 并且它一直深受安圭拉人民的喜爱。

sentences.en: The flag was raised over the administrative office, along with the Union Jack, a clear declaration of independence and dependence at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这面旗帜与米字旗一起在行政办公楼上空升起，这既是对独立的明确宣言，也是对依附的宣告。

sentences.en: As a graphic designer, my father had been really proud of the work that he had done for the island.
sentences.zh: 作为一名平面设计师，我父亲为这座岛屿所做的工作感到由衷的骄傲。

sentences.en: But Alan Gumbs remembers it a different way.
sentences.zh: 但艾伦·甘布斯有不同的回忆。

sentences.en: It was my mother was the art, you know, I had the imagination.
sentences.zh: 艺术部分是我母亲，你知道的，我负责想象力。

sentences.en: And she was the one that came up with the three dolphins.
sentences.zh: 三只海豚是她想出来的。

sentences.en: And there was somebody who helped her draw it.
sentences.zh: 当时有人帮她画了出来。

sentences.en: And that was it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Gumbs is positive that his mother Lydia was actually the designer of the famous dolphin flag of Anguilla.
sentences.zh: 甘布斯坚信他的母亲莉迪亚实际上才是著名的安圭拉海豚旗的设计者。

sentences.en: If she was, she might have been working with Mr. Olbermann, you know, not impossible.
sentences.zh: 如果真是她，她可能曾与奥尔伯曼先生合作过，你知道的，这并非不可能。

sentences.en: Most Anguillians who know the revolutionary history will probably tell you that Lydia designed the flag.
sentences.zh: 大多数了解这段革命历史的安圭拉人可能会告诉你，旗帜是莉迪亚设计的。

sentences.en: While flag nerds who read the September 1991 issue of the flag bulletin will probably tell you that Marvin was the designer.
sentences.zh: 而那些阅读过1991年9月版《旗帜公报》的旗帜迷们可能会告诉你，马文才是设计者。

sentences.en: The truth may actually lie somewhere in between.
sentences.zh: 真相其实可能介于两者之间。

sentences.en: But as a successful graphic designer herself, Emily has a healthy perspective on the debate.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名成功的平面设计师，艾米莉对这场争论有着健康的看法。

sentences.en: I have always believed, and I usually think about this in terms of my team, but I can say this in terms of clients as well.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为，我通常会从我的团队角度来考虑这个问题，但我也可以从客户的角度来说。

sentences.en: To me, a project that is successful is one where everyone who worked on the project thinks that they were 100% responsible for it.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，一个成功的项目是，所有参与这个项目的每个人都认为自己对它负有百分之百的责任。

sentences.en: Regardless of who designed it, the Anguillians had a flag and a revolutionary spirit.
sentences.zh: 无论是谁设计的，安圭拉人拥有了一面旗帜和一种革命精神。

sentences.en: But they were still stuck in this confusing tangle of colonial bureaucracy,
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然陷入了殖民官僚主义这令人困惑的纠葛之中，

sentences.en: since they were fighting for independence from St. Kitts, but not from Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是在争取脱离圣基茨独立，而不是脱离英国。

sentences.en: Revolutionary leaders tried to negotiate a direct relationship with Britain,
sentences.zh: 革命领袖试图与英国建立直接关系，

sentences.en: but Britain refused to deal with Anguilla without going through St. Kitts firSt.
sentences.zh: 但英国拒绝在不通过圣基茨的情况下与安圭拉打交道。

sentences.en: Anguilla did not want to do that, and so the tension just continued to escalate.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉不愿意这样做，因此紧张局势继续升级。

sentences.en: But even with this tension, it remained a bloodless conflict.
sentences.zh: 但尽管有这种紧张局势，这仍然是一场没有流血的冲突。

sentences.en: The man who eventually became known as the father of the nation in Anguilla, Ronald Webster,
sentences.zh: 后来被称为安圭拉国父的罗纳德·韦伯斯特，

sentences.en: said, oh, the revolution was really a war of words.
sentences.zh: 曾说，哦，这场革命实际上是一场言语之战。

sentences.en: Here's Don Wolachek again.
sentences.zh: 这是唐·沃拉切克的再次讲述。

sentences.en: He meant that he won a lot of battles with words, with threats, with conversations with reporters.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，他通过言语、威胁以及与记者的对话赢得了许多战斗。

sentences.en: The media was captivated by the story of this tiny island in a territorial dispute
sentences.zh: 媒体被这个陷入领土争端的微小岛屿的故事深深吸引，

sentences.en: with one of the most powerful nations in the world.
sentences.zh: 而对手是世界上最强大的国家之一。

sentences.en: One can only die once.
sentences.zh: 人只能死一次。

sentences.en: He can only die once.
sentences.zh: 他只能死一次。

sentences.en: And we are prepared to die for our freedom.
sentences.zh: 我们已经准备好为自由而死。

sentences.en: This is the voice of revolutionary leader Ronald Webster,
sentences.zh: 这是革命领袖罗纳德·韦伯斯特的声音，

sentences.en: who, along with Jeremiah Gumbs, petitioned the United Nations to back the Anguillian cause.
sentences.zh: 他与杰里米亚·甘布斯一起向联合国请愿，支持安圭拉的事业。

sentences.en: They failed to convince the UN, but their story was in papers all over the world.
sentences.zh: 他们没能说服联合国，但他们的故事登上了世界各地的报纸。

sentences.en: The press were now following my father, because Anguilla had become the mouse that roared,
sentences.zh: 记者们现在开始关注我父亲，因为安圭拉已经成了“发出怒吼的小老鼠”，

sentences.en: and they were in the New York Times every day for months.
sentences.zh: 而且他们连续几个月每天都出现在《纽约时报》上。

sentences.en: The Mouse That Roared was a satirical novel by Leonard Wiberly about a tiny nation that declares war on the U.S.
sentences.zh: 《发出怒吼的小老鼠》是伦纳德·威伯利的一部讽刺小说，讲述了一个对美国宣战的小国的故事。

sentences.en: The reporters couldn't help but see an ironic similarity between the two situations.
sentences.zh: 记者们不禁在这两种情况之间看到了具有讽刺意味的相似之处。

sentences.en: Anguilla was this surprisingly ferocious island that refused to back down.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉就是这样一个令人惊叹的、凶猛且拒绝退缩的岛屿。

sentences.en: Anguilla was this small place lurking in the corner that no one thought could produce such a giant, powerful political movement.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉是那个潜伏在角落里的小地方，没有人想到它能产生如此庞大、强大的政治运动。

sentences.en: And it surprised everybody.
sentences.zh: 这让所有人都感到惊讶。

sentences.en: You know, the movement was heard all over the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这场运动的声音传遍了全世界。

sentences.en: More than anything, the revolution marked a huge shift in what it really meant to be an Anguillian.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，这场革命标志着安圭拉人身份认同的巨大转变。

sentences.en: And it united Anguillians behind a single purpose, under a single flag.
sentences.zh: 它将安圭拉人团结在单一的目标下，在同一面旗帜下。

sentences.en: But despite this new unity, St. Kitts still had the power.
sentences.zh: 但尽管有了这种新的团结，圣基茨仍然掌握着权力。

sentences.en: And they were withholding everything from postcards to pensions.
sentences.zh: 他们扣留了一切，从明信片到养老金。

sentences.en: The leader of St. Kitts, Robert Bradshaw, even reportedly said,
sentences.zh: 据报道，圣基茨领导人罗伯特·布拉德肖甚至说过，

sentences.en: quote,
sentences.zh: 引述，

sentences.en: I must get Anguilla back on their knees, end quote.
sentences.zh: 我一定要让安圭拉人重新屈服，引述结束。

sentences.en: Britain had no intention of separating the two islands, and Anguillians were losing their patience.
sentences.zh: 英国无意将两岛分离，安圭拉人正在失去耐心。

sentences.en: They realized they were being strung along.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到自己被耍了。

sentences.en: And they realized that Britain wasn't particularly invested in allowing them to determine their own destiny.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到英国并不怎么关心让他们决定自己的命运。

sentences.en: So in February of 1969, two years after Anguilla declared independence from the Associated State,
sentences.zh: 因此，在1969年2月，即安圭拉宣布脱离联系邦两年后，

sentences.en: it took a more drastic step and declared independence again.
sentences.zh: 它采取了更激进的一步，再次宣布独立。

sentences.en: But this time, it was from the British.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，对象是英国人。

sentences.en: As a tiny nation with no diplomatic recognition, this was an incredibly risky move.
sentences.zh: 作为一个没有外交承认的微型国家，这是一个极其冒险的举动。

sentences.en: But Anguillians voted 1,739 to 4 to end all ties with Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 但安圭拉人以1739票对4票投票决定切断与英国的所有联系。

sentences.en: The Union Jack that had flowed alongside the dolphin flag since the start of the revolution
sentences.zh: 自革命开始以来一直与海豚旗并肩飘扬的米字旗

sentences.en: was taken down because they decided they would rather try to make it entirely on their own
sentences.zh: 被降了下来，因为他们决定宁愿完全靠自己闯出一片天，

sentences.en: than to have any connection with St. Kitts.
sentences.zh: 也不愿与圣基茨有任何联系。

sentences.en: They would never negotiate that.
sentences.zh: 他们绝不会就此进行谈判。

sentences.en: They said they will never be part of the Associated State in the discussion.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，绝不会在讨论中成为联系邦的一部分。

sentences.en: But Britain wasn't ready to let go.
sentences.zh: 但英国并不准备放手。

sentences.en: And they attempted a last-ditch effort to save the Associated State.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了最后一次挽救联系邦的尝试。

sentences.en: They sent a British representative to Anguilla named William Whitlock
sentences.zh: 他们派了一位名叫威廉·惠特洛克的英国代表前往安圭拉，

sentences.en: to try to negotiate with the Anguillians.
sentences.zh: 试图与安圭拉人谈判。

sentences.en: You have to understand, you're dealing with the dead-and-dying vestiges of the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，你打交道的是大英帝国行将就木的残余势力。

sentences.en: They didn't necessarily send their brightest people out to the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 他们未必会把最聪明的人派到加勒比海去。

sentences.en: The accounts of what happened next tend to vary depending on whether you're asking an Anguillian
sentences.zh: 接下来的事情经过，根据你问的是安圭拉人

sentences.en: or a British person.
sentences.zh: 还是英国人，往往会有所不同。

sentences.en: But according to Walachek, the Anguillians welcomed Whitlock at the airport
sentences.zh: 但据沃拉切克说，安圭拉人在机场迎接惠特洛克时，

sentences.en: with a stirring rendition of God Save the Queen.
sentences.zh: 深情地合唱了《天佑女王》。

sentences.en: And as a sign of respect to Whitlock, Ronald Webster, the Anguillian leader,
sentences.zh: 作为对惠特洛克的尊重，安圭拉领导人罗纳德·韦伯斯特

sentences.en: came dressed to the nines.
sentences.zh: 特意盛装打扮。

sentences.en: He was actually wearing, what do you call it, a dinner coat?
sentences.zh: 他实际上穿了，怎么说呢，一件晚礼服？

sentences.en: A very formal, sort of, I'm not British, right?
sentences.zh: 非常正式的那种，有点像，我不是英国人，对吧？

sentences.en: This thing that British people know what it is, right?
sentences.zh: 英国人一看就知道是什么的那种东西，对吧？

sentences.en: He's dressed in this, like it had a tail.
sentences.zh: 他穿着这个，好像还带着燕尾。

sentences.en: But the courtesy wasn't returned.
sentences.zh: 但这种礼貌并没有得到回报。

sentences.en: Apparently Whitlock blew off an invitation to have lunch with Webster
sentences.zh: 显然，惠特洛克拒绝了与韦伯斯特共进午餐的邀请，

sentences.en: and instead ate with another British official stationed on the island.
sentences.zh: 而是与另一位驻扎在岛上的英国官员一起吃了饭。

sentences.en: Feeling disrespected, the Anguillians asked Whitlock to leave the island.
sentences.zh: 安圭拉人感到不受尊重，便要求惠特洛克离开该岛。

sentences.en: And he says, well, you know, you can't throw, I represent the crown,
sentences.zh: 而他说，好吧，你知道的，你不能赶，我代表王室，

sentences.en: so you can't throw me, you can't tell me to leave.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能赶我走，你不能让我离开。

sentences.en: But the Anguillians were having none of it.
sentences.zh: 但安圭拉人根本不吃这一套。

sentences.en: I believe they fired some guns into the air to signal that they were serious.
sentences.zh: 我记得到处有人朝空中鸣枪，以示他们是认真的。

sentences.en: Whitlock jumped on a plane with his tail between his legs
sentences.zh: 惠特洛克夹着尾巴跳上一架飞机，

sentences.en: and headed straight back to Britain.
sentences.zh: 径直返回了英国。

sentences.en: Whitlock was humiliated.
sentences.zh: 惠特洛克受到了羞辱。

sentences.en: He shared his humiliation with his peers and his superiors.
sentences.zh: 他向他的同僚和上级倾诉了自己的羞辱。

sentences.en: It's not really clear if he exaggerated what happened,
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚他是否夸大了事情的经过，

sentences.en: but he really portrayed the islanders as villains
sentences.zh: 但他确实把岛民描绘成了一群

sentences.en: who were extremely violent and about to kill him.
sentences.zh: 极其暴力并且即将杀害他的恶棍。

sentences.en: Britain decided the only way to respond
sentences.zh: 英国决定唯一的应对方式

sentences.en: was by mounting a full-scale invasion to restore order.
sentences.zh: 就是发起一场全面入侵以恢复秩序。

sentences.en: So the British invasion, such as you want to call it, actually occurred.
sentences.zh: 所以英国的入侵，如果你想这么称呼的话，真的发生了。

sentences.en: They sent a frigate down there.
sentences.zh: 他们派了一艘护卫舰过去。

sentences.en: Two Royal Navy frigates arrived and 330 paratroopers.
sentences.zh: 两艘英国皇家海军护卫舰和330名伞兵抵达了。

sentences.en: People talk about seeing, you know, jeeps coming out of the sky.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论着看到吉普车从天而降的场景。
